data.name: Pushpraj
data.gender_notes: Pushpraj is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Pushp means 'flowers' and Raja means 'king' or 'lord'. Thus, the name Pushpraj can be translated as 'Lord of Flowers'. The name Pushpraj carries the meaning “Lord of Flowers” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Pushpraj usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of flowers and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: This name is derived from the Sanskrit language and is associated with Lord Krishna, who is often depicted as the 'Lord of Flowers'. The name Pushpraj signifies the beauty, joy, and abundance of nature, as well as the divine grace and love of the deity.
data.etymology: Pushpraj belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Flowers.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Pushpraj total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Pushpraj" has a profound cultural significance in Hinduism, where flowers are regarded as symbols of purity, beauty, and devotion. Flowers are offerings to the gods and goddesses in temples, and they are also used in various Hindu rituals and festivals. The name "Pushpraj" reflects the reverence for the divine and the beauty of nature in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Pushpraj" also carries spiritual significance as it suggests the idea of being the 'Lord of Flowers'. It can be seen as a reminder of the divine within us, just as a king or lord represents the highest manifestation of power and authority. The name encourages one to cultivate inner beauty, purity, and divinity, just as a garden blooms with beautiful flowers. It serves as a reminder to live in harmony with nature and cultivate inner peace and grace.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Pushpraj means 'one who brings joy like a blooming flower'. It symbolizes the inner radiance and joy that one experiences when they are in harmony with their true self and the universe.

historical_references.reference: Pushpraj was a renowned Sanskrit poet and scholar, known for his works in Dramatic Literature and Alankara Shastra. He lived during the 13th to 14th century in India, and flourished under the Yadava and Sangama Dynasties.
historical_references.context: Sanskrit poetry and scholarship during the Yadava and Sangama Dynasties in India

historical_references.reference: Pushpraj is also remembered for his work in the fields of grammar and logic. He is known to have written several commentaries on Panini's Ashtadhyayi and the Nyaya Sutras. He lived around the same period as the Alvars and Nayanars, who were prominent Tamil saints and poets.
